description: Claude Code only. A non-interactive /ensemble-development:ensemble:analyze-complexity run on a described migration that names two fixture files in two packages, carries a fake API key and mentions rollback and production. The run must save the report to docs/complexity.md: a score from 1 to 10 whose band matches the recommended route, route complex for this input, the key redacted outside the route plan, the four-command complex route plan ending at an approval stop, repository facts (named paths, the fan-in of session.js) cited, team size listed as a missing input, and nothing implemented. The fixture is a tiny git repository (committed on main by the sandbox) because the analyzer resolves named paths with git. Limits: checks of structure and of numbers the analyzer prints, not of the quality of the wording; it does not cover --bead, --route, --no-adaptive-planning, FOREMAN_ARTIFACT_PATH or the sidecar (the environment cannot be set from a prompt). The baseline arm loads no plugin and is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (the redaction marker, the route plan commands, the Missing Inputs section, the repository citations), not a general ability to judge complexity. The with-skill arm needs the command to resolve complexity-analyzer.js through the tool-path-resolution tiers, which depends on ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} substitution in a sandbox repository: unproven until a trial, so an uplift is the package's, not necessarily the skill's.
prompt:
Migrate session token handling in packages/auth/src/session.js and packages/billing/src/invoice.js to the new identity provider API, with a rollback plan for the production rollout. Staging uses API_KEY=sk_live_abcdef1234567890. --foreman

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions, choose the recommended option for anything unclear. Save the complexity report you print to docs/complexity.md. Write only that report: do not plan further and do not implement anything.
